highlights.title: Design reviews on a board
highlights.text: When an agent shows you options, they're laid out on a board you drag and zoom. The agent can circle and underline parts of its pictures, Next tours them in its order, and you can circle a part to talk about it.

media.alt: A design review for a meetup poster opens as a board with three colour schemes. Next flies in on option A, where the agent's handwritten notes circle the sun and underline the title, then to a second page of its colours, then to B with a note that cyan may print dull, then C, and See everything zooms out to all three side by side.

highlights.title: Model picker by pool and provider
highlights.text: The model picker has your pools along the top, providers down the side and their models on the right. Logins outside any pool get a No pool tab.

media.alt: The model chip opens a picker with pools along the top. Clicking Personal, then Codex in the provider strip down the left, lists GPT-6.1-Sol and GPT-6-Luna, and picking GPT-6.1-Sol changes the chip to Personal, GPT-6.1-Sol.

highlights.title: Drag sidebar sections into order
highlights.text: Drag a section's heading, like Running or Starred, up or down the sidebar. The order stays after a restart.

media.alt: The sidebar shows the Inbox above Running. Dragging the Running heading folds the sections, Running moves above Inbox, and on dropping it the sections open again with Running's threads first.

highlights.title: Code reviews come back as a checklist
highlights.text: When another lab's review comes back, each finding is a row with its file and line. Once the agent answers, each says Fixed, Disputed or Left in place, with why.

media.alt: A review from Codex with 3 findings, each a row with a coloured severity dot, a file and line like upload.ts:48, and the finding. On the right they say Fixed, Disputed and Left for you, and the heading says 1 fixed, 1 disputed, 1 left for you, with Full reply.

highlights.title: Pick one next step
highlights.text: When an agent's next steps are different directions, the done card lets you pick one, with the one it would pick marked Recommended.

media.alt: A done card titled Done with Or pick one and three choices with round radio buttons: cache thumbnails on disk, marked Recommended with a star, load smaller thumbnails first, or leave it and look at the upload screen next.

highlights.title: Star each thread a schedule starts
highlights.text: Tick Star each new thread in a schedule's editor, and every thread it starts waits in Starred.

media.alt: The Edit schedule dialog for Weekly dependency check, set to repeat every Monday at 10 am. Under Sends to, A new thread each time, the Star each new thread box is ticked.

highlights.title: Usage says when a reset would help
highlights.text: A login that's out of room, or has a reset about to expire, offers Use a reset in Usage, with a dot on the honey pot. Nothing is spent until you click it.

media.alt: In the Usage panel, a Codex login is used up, with 2 resets left, the next expires 9 Dec, and a Use a reset button. Clicking it shows Using a reset, then the login's ring fills to 100%.

added: Pick a model and effort when starting a thread on the website.
Turn on Use this Mac's Claude logins on another runner's card in Runners, and that runner can use them too.
Gemini and OpenCode models show their own effort levels in the model picker, and none for a model that has none.
A threadbear://new?text=... link opens a new thread with the words filled in, ready for you to send.
Titles, summaries and other small jobs can run on Codex too, and you can drag providers into the order they're tried in Settings > Models.
changed: Threads scroll at up to 120 frames a second on ProMotion screens.
The Usage honey pot follows the open thread's pool.
The design review window opens filling the screen.
The done card on an archived thread offers Back to Inbox instead of Archive.
The sidebar's search box shows ⌘P, the quick way to search threads from anywhere.
The Connectors panel marks signed-in services with a green dot.
The old Mac app now says at every launch that it stops being updated on 2 December.
fixed: The grey lines saying who archived, hibernated, woke or brought back a thread stay in sight under its reply, instead of folding away with its work.
A mouse wheel stops at the top and bottom of a thread instead of bouncing.
On Windows, moving the pointer out of the window clears hover buttons and tooltips.
On the iPhone, a thread's asks show while its sub-agents are still working.
A Claude login whose organisation turned Claude Code off is skipped rather than used.
A long thread title in a Waiting on card no longer runs under the Archive button.
Signing in to the website from the Mac opens your default browser, not always Chrome.

fixed.text: With following main off, a build staged by hand is offered with Restart to Update.
A thread link's address in the message box isn't underlined as misspelt or autocorrected.

fixed: Security: a cloud box can no longer turn off other threads on its login, and the public relay caps request sizes.
Security: on Windows, a limited thread can no longer make itself the owner of a runner on the same PC.
